headline: Cristiano Ronaldo provisionally suspended by Portugal after team walkout
summary: The Portuguese Football Federation has opened disciplinary proceedings against the 41-year-old forward following a dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus.
details: The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has provisionally suspended Cristiano Ronaldo after he left the national team camp in Copenhagen.
The incident occurred before a Nations League match against Denmark last week, following a heated dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus.
Ronaldo, who remained an unused substitute during a previous game against Norway, accused the coach of breaking his word regarding his role in the team.
According to Portuguese media, the FPF has given the disciplinary proceedings urgent status and implemented a non-automatic preventive suspension.
Ronaldo has since apologized for leaving his teammates and for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match.
The forward stated that he remains available for selection once he has served any punishment resulting from the incident.
caption:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended from the Portugal national team after walking out of the squad base.

The Portuguese Football Federation (FPF) has provisionally suspended Cristiano Ronaldo after he left the national team camp in Copenhagen.

The incident occurred before a Nations League match against Denmark last week, following a heated dispute with head coach Jorge Jesus.

Ronaldo, who remained an unused substitute during a previous game against Norway, accused the coach of breaking his word regarding his role in the team.

According to Portuguese media, the FPF has given the disciplinary proceedings urgent status and implemented a non-automatic preventive suspension.

Ronaldo has since apologized for leaving his teammates and for failing to acknowledge supporters after the Norway match.

The forward stated that he remains available for selection once he has served any punishment resulting from the incident.

headline_marked: Elon Musk announces [[Starlink Mobile now available in Bangladesh]]
headline: Elon Musk announces Starlink Mobile now available in Bangladesh
summary: Bangladesh becomes the first South Asian country to introduce satellite-to-mobile connectivity via Banglalink.
details: Elon Musk shared the news on X, announcing that Starlink Mobile is now available in Bangladesh. His post, which highlighted the service's launch with Banglalink, has already garnered millions of views.
The satellite-to-mobile service allows millions of customers to message through apps, share their locations, and stay connected in cellular dead zones using compatible 4G phones.
Banglalink stated that Bangladesh is the first country in South Asia to introduce this technology, which connects mobile phones directly to satellites, bypassing conventional cellular towers.
The service is specifically designed to help people stay connected during emergencies, natural disasters, and prolonged power outages when traditional networks are disrupted.
It is particularly aimed at fishermen, sea-farers, and residents of remote and coastal areas, including deep-sea locations within Bangladesh's Exclusive Economic Zone.
Access is free for the first month with any internet or mixed bundle, and continues at no additional cost with selected monthly packs. Users also receive five free satellite SMS messages each month.
caption:
Elon Musk just announced it: Starlink Mobile is officially live in Bangladesh!

Elon Musk shared the news on X, announcing that Starlink Mobile is now available in Bangladesh. His post, which highlighted the service's launch with Banglalink, has already garnered millions of views.

The satellite-to-mobile service allows millions of customers to message through apps, share their locations, and stay connected in cellular dead zones using compatible 4G phones.

Banglalink stated that Bangladesh is the first country in South Asia to introduce this technology, which connects mobile phones directly to satellites, bypassing conventional cellular towers.

The service is specifically designed to help people stay connected during emergencies, natural disasters, and prolonged power outages when traditional networks are disrupted.

It is particularly aimed at fishermen, sea-farers, and residents of remote and coastal areas, including deep-sea locations within Bangladesh's Exclusive Economic Zone.

Access is free for the first month with any internet or mixed bundle, and continues at no additional cost with selected monthly packs. Users also receive five free satellite SMS messages each month.
